question: Let $A$ be the set of all functions $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ such that $f(xy)=xf(y)$ for all $x,y\in\mathbb{R}$. (a) If $f\in A$, then show that $f(x+y)=f(x)+f(y)$ for all $x,y\in\mathbb{R}$. (b) For $g,h\in A$, define a function $g\circ h$ by $(g\circ h)(x)=g(h(x))$ for $x\in\mathbb{R}$. Prove that $g\circ h$ is in $A$ and is equal to $h\circ g$.

source.title: Test of Mathematics at the 10 + 2 Level
